newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs fall, mogas, fuel flat.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs fall, mogas, fuel flat.

text.p: Brent CFD swaps were battered again on Wednesday as support for prompt contracts levelled out and the bearish market took its toll, but other oil swaps were broadly steady, traders said.

Brent CFDs tripped up and fell down to -4.00 cents against July for the balance of this week compared with +4.00 yesterday. Traders said support for prompt contracts was evaporating after good trader support late last week and early this week.
Further out contracts also took a pasting with June 2-6 sliding to -29 cents from -22.5 cents, and June 9-13 down to -27 cents from -22.5. Dealers said there were few bids for next week, only offers.

High sulphur fuel oil swaps were about $1-2 a tonne higher with talk around $82.00 on June and $83.50 on July after early morning physical barges went for as low as $77 and $77.50 fob ARA in a Russian cargo pricing manoeuvre.
Low sulphur June swaps were heard done twice at $95 with July showing a $1 contango.

Gasoline was steady at $204-205 for June, seeking direction from the U.S. market. Business was concluded at $204 and $204.50 for June, with July pegged at around $198/$199 fob ARA. Traders said the delay to the U.K. budget, in which many traders expected a rise in gasoline duty, had pulled the rug from under market bulls.

Naphtha was a touch firmer amid talk that crude's recent fall was overdone and June swaps were traded at $189, with July talked at $189.50. Many dealers were concentrating on the latest six-month Egyptian tender which closed on Wednesday.
